answer: Lotus employs delta-stake verification, where each node must commit delta-stake to validate transactions, ensuring Sybil resistance. An attacker deploying more Sybil nodes incurs a capital lockup of (N-1)delta per node, where N is the number of nodes. This leads to a strictly negative expected utility as the cost exceeds potential rewards. Zenith's verifiable delay function further mitigates this by enforcing a computational bottleneck, sustaining Byzantine Fault Tolerance through this economic and cryptographic defense.
